title: The Old Hound
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Hound who had served his master well for years, and had run down many a quarry in his time, began to lose his strength and speed owing to age. One day, when out hunting, his master started a powerful wild boar and set the Hound at him. The latter seized the beast by the ear, but his teeth were gone and he could not retain his hold; so the boar escaped. His master began to scold him severely, but the Hound interrupted him with these words: "My will is as strong as ever, master, but my body is old and feeble. You ought to honour me for what I have been instead of abusing me for what I am."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what has the Hound done for his master over the years?
options: Guarded the house through every night
Herded the sheep across the farm
Served him well and run down many a quarry
Carried heavy loads on long journeys

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what has begun to happen to the Hound because of his age?
options: He has begun to lose his strength and speed
He has begun to lose his sense of smell
He has begun to refuse hunting altogether
He has begun to sleep through the daylight hours

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the master's Hound seize during the hunt?
options: The boar's hind leg
A smaller animal fleeing nearby
The master's fallen weapon
The wild boar by the ear

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Hound lose his grip on the boar?
options: He is distracted by a noise nearby
His teeth were gone and he could not retain his hold
The boar is far larger than any he had faced before
His master calls him away too soon

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the master react when the boar escapes?
options: He comforts the Hound gently
He blames himself for the failure
He scolds the Hound severely
He decides to retire the Hound at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hound say about his will compared to his body?
options: His will is as strong as ever, but his body is old and feeble
Both his will and his body have grown weak together
His will has weakened faster than his body
Neither his will nor his body have changed at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hound ask his master to honour him for?
options: The size of the boar he almost caught
The number of years he has left to serve
The training his master once gave him
What he has been, rather than what he is now

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Hound's failure with the boar not really a matter of unwillingness?
options: He deliberately let the boar go to avoid injury
His effort was genuine, but his aging body could no longer carry it out
He was never actually trained to hunt boars
He was distracted by another animal during the chase

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "quarry" mean in "had run down many a quarry in his time"?
options: A stone pit used for building
A type of hunting weapon
An animal being hunted
A place where dogs are trained

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Past service deserves recognition even when age limits present performance
Hunting dogs should be replaced as soon as they grow old
Willpower alone is always enough to overcome physical decline
Masters should never scold their animals under any circumstances

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the master hunting on the day of the story?
options: A fleeing stag
A pack of wolves
A large bear
A powerful wild boar

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of the Hound's body specifically fails him during the chase?
options: His legs
His teeth
His eyesight
His hearing

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Hound respond to his master's scolding?
options: By running away in shame
By staying silent and accepting the blame
By interrupting him with an explanation
By attacking the boar again immediately

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Hound want his master to remember about their relationship?
options: The years of loyal, successful service before his decline
That he was never truly a skilled hunter
That the master trained him poorly from the start
That the boar was simply too fast for any dog

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the master's scolding be seen as unfair?
options: It comes from a master who has never hunted himself
It happens in front of other hunting dogs
It follows a mistake the Hound made deliberately
It ignores the natural limits of age after years of loyal service

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "feeble" mean in "my body is old and feeble"?
options: Injured
Weak
Untrained
Impatient

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A young Hound is praised for catching a boar with ease
A Hound refuses to hunt and is punished by his master
An aging Hound defends his years of service after failing to hold a boar
A master retires his Hound before any hunt takes place
